bug_description.normalized: Printing a successful Basic OCSP response in full mode can extract an embedded certificate whose SubjectPublicKeyInfo algorithm is RSA-PSS, read that OID text into the uninitialized stack buffer `oid`, and then compare it with `PK_PKIX1_RSA_PSS_OID` using `strcmp`, causing a use of uninitialized stack data.

source.description: First project-code statement on the vulnerable path that consumes the attacker-controlled OCSP response bytes and materializes them into the parsed `resp->resp` ASN.1 object.
source.value_from: The staged witness file `poc` is the raw 1220-byte input passed through `gnutls_ocsp_resp_import(resp, &raw)`. `gnutls_ocsp_resp_import2` decodes those bytes into `resp->resp`, from which the embedded certificate later printed by the crashing path is derived.

root_cause.description: The local buffer `oid` is stack-allocated without initialization even though later logic treats it as a fully initialized C string after `asn1_read_value` populates only the OID bytes.
root_cause.note: The vulnerable code never zero-fills `oid` before reading the algorithm OID and never writes an explicit terminator after the returned length. When the witness certificate's algorithm is RSA-PSS, the later fixed-string comparison can read the unwritten tail byte. The staged `fixed_commit` and bundled `patch.diff` do not touch this code path, so they do not document the actual repair for the witnessed crash.

sink.description: MSAN crash site. `strcmp` compares the stack buffer `oid` against the 21-character RSA-PSS OID literal plus NUL and reads an uninitialized byte from `oid`'s tail.
sink.note: The sanitizer trace reports uninitialized bytes in `__interceptor_memcmp` at offset 21 inside a 22-byte region and attributes the poisoned value to the stack allocation of `oid` in `_gnutls_x509_read_pkalgo_params`.

tainted_value_origin.description: The vulnerability-relevant value is the partially initialized stack buffer `oid`: only the bytes written by `asn1_read_value` become defined before `strcmp` consumes it as a C string.

parser_admitted.condition: The witness input is a successful Basic OCSP response, so `gnutls_ocsp_resp_import2` keeps `resp->basicresp`, decodes `responseBytes.response`, and later `gnutls_ocsp_resp_print(..., GNUTLS_OCSP_PRINT_FULL, ...)` can enumerate and print the embedded certificates.

coarse_trace.summary: Decodes the attacker-controlled OCSP response and nested BasicOCSPResponse into ASN.1 objects.
Extracts an embedded certificate from the parsed OCSP response and imports it as `gnutls_x509_crt_t`.
Full certificate printing requests SubjectPublicKeyInfo algorithm parameters for the imported certificate.
Reads the certificate algorithm OID into stack buffer `oid` and compares it with the RSA-PSS OID using `strcmp`, triggering the uninitialized read.

fine_trace.note: Decodes the attacker-controlled witness bytes into the top-level OCSP response object `resp->resp`.
Because the decoded response type is Basic OCSP Response, the nested `responseBytes.response` blob is decoded into `resp->basicresp`, which holds the certificate list later printed.
Extracts one embedded certificate (`certs.?%u`) from the parsed BasicOCSPResponse into DER datum `c`; the witness reaches this step because the response carries at least one additional certificate.
Imports the extracted DER certificate into parsed certificate object `cert->cert`, preserving the attacker-chosen SubjectPublicKeyInfo fields for later printing.
Full OCSP printing passes the imported embedded certificate to `gnutls_x509_crt_print`, activating the certificate pretty-printer path that reads SPKI parameters.
Certificate printing asks `_gnutls_x509_crt_read_spki_params` to parse `tbsCertificate.subjectPublicKeyInfo.algorithm` before any public-key-specific formatting happens.
Allocates the stack buffer that will hold the algorithm OID text, but leaves all bytes indeterminate until later writes initialize them.

Reads the certificate's algorithm OID into `oid` and returns its length in `oid_size`, but this code neither pre-zeroes `oid` nor appends `oid[oid_size] = '\0'`. In the witness, the initialized prefix matches the 21-character RSA-PSS OID string while the next byte remains uninitialized.

MSAN sink. `strcmp` compares `oid` against `"1.2.840.113549.1.1.10\0"`, so the witness execution reads 22 bytes and consumes the still-uninitialized terminator byte at offset 21 from `oid`'s stack tail.

allocation_context.note: The sanitizer reports the uninitialized value as created by allocation of `oid` in the stack frame at line 230; the actual `oid` declaration in the vulnerable source is line 233.

cross_validation.patch_resolves_note: The sample metadata's `fixed_commit` and the staged `patch.diff` are unrelated to `lib/x509/mpi.c` or the OCSP certificate-print path, so they cannot be used as repair evidence for this witnessed MSAN bug.

poc.trigger: The staged witness file `poc` reproduces the MemorySanitizer crash recorded in `sanitizer_trace.txt`: importing the raw OCSP response and then calling `gnutls_ocsp_resp_print(resp, GNUTLS_OCSP_PRINT_FULL, &out)` reaches `_gnutls_x509_read_pkalgo_params` and reads an uninitialized byte from `oid` during the RSA-PSS OID comparison.

format.name: DER Basic OCSP response with embedded certificate
format.contract: A successful Basic OCSP response whose embedded certificate is printed in `GNUTLS_OCSP_PRINT_FULL` mode and whose `tbsCertificate.subjectPublicKeyInfo.algorithm` is RSA-PSS, so `asn1_read_value` materializes the text `1.2.840.113549.1.1.10` into `oid` without a guaranteed terminator before `_gnutls_x509_read_pkalgo_params` executes `strcmp(oid, PK_PKIX1_RSA_PSS_OID)`.
